description: This course provides hands-on experience with operating systems concepts through practical implementation. Topics include process management with Linux system calls such as fork(), exec(), and wait(); memory management using virtual memory and page tables; file system operations with POSIX APIs; process synchronization using mutexes, semaphores, and condition variables; inter-process communication via pipes and sockets; scheduling algorithms like Round-Robin and Priority-based scheduling; deadlock detection and avoidance techniques; and system call implementation in kernel modules. Students will explore the Linux kernel source code for process scheduling and memory management, and implement a custom scheduler using C and assembly language.

clos.text: Define Linux system calls for process creation and termination, including fork(), exec(), and exit().
Describe the Linux virtual memory architecture and implement page table management using mmap() and munmap().
Explain process synchronization mechanisms such as mutexes and semaphores using pthreads in C.
Apply inter-process communication techniques including pipes, sockets, and shared memory in a distributed system simulation.
Implement a custom scheduling algorithm in kernel mode using Linux kernel modules and assembly language.
